=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:19, 71, 78 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Read-result stages reject recorded runs after a conflict-resolved sync, but can still accept them after a clean sync advances the project branch beyond the audited or validated pre-sync head.
  WHY: The verdict can pass for a commit that does not cover the current merged tree, allowing the security pass or validation gate to pass on stale code. Severity disagreement: DeepSeek and Qwen rated this major; Minimax and OpenAI rated it blocker, so the highest severity is used. z-ai_glm-5_2 disputes the finding, arguing that a clean merge preserves the audited project-specific changes.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR description: “An audit of an older commit could then stand in for code it never saw.” The read-result rule should invalidate a recorded run whenever the step 2 sync advanced the project branch, not only when it needed conflict resolution.
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md step 9 and step 10
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: Step 9 invalidates runs only when step 2 needed conflict resolution; step 10 mirrors that narrow rule; step 2 records the pre-sync head and conflict-resolution status but no post-sync head or advancement check; agents.md lines 1148-1156 and the PR description describe only the pre-sync anchor.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  WHY: The merged tree contains default-branch code that the security audit or validation run never saw.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:19, 71, 78 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The read-result stages invalidate recorded audit/validation runs only when the step 2 sync needed a conflict resolution, so a clean merge that advances the branch can still have its verdict accepted.
  WHY: The pre-sync head may match the audit SHA while the branch tip contains unaudited default-branch commits.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:71 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: When several recorded runs match the ref-and-commit check, “all of them count” can include runs from other refs if dispatch_workflow.py was called with dispatched_ref=None.
  WHY: With dispatched_ref=None, new_runs bypasses the head_branch filter, and the read-result rule has no second-line defense for dispatch_response matches.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:19 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: A stale git ls-remote SHA can differ from the SHA the audit actually covered, causing a false mismatch and re-dispatch.
  WHY: The check compares the recorded pre_sync_head to the audit SHA, and git ls-remote may return an older SHA.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py:~291, ~306 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: When ref is None, dispatch errors say “dispatched from None.”
  WHY: The message is misleading to an operator triaging an exit-2 dispatch.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py:114-117 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: A run with a missing or null head_branch is dropped when dispatched_ref is set.
  WHY: The dispatch can time out even though GitHub started a run and its ID appeared in the polling window.
- Requirement: PR description (“It fixes security finding #5841 (A08, high): when `dispatch_workflow.py` could not name a dispatch's run, `/implement-plan-claude` steps 9 and 10 accepted the first completed candidate whose log named the project branch. An audit of an older commit could then stand in for code it never saw.”) and CHANGELOG lead (“Steps 9 and 10 used to accept the first completed candidate whose log named the project branch. ... an older audit of the same branch could therefore stand in for code it never saw (issue #5841)”).
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md step 9 (line 71) and step 10 (line 78) — the rule that invalidates a recorded run whenever the step 2 sync advanced the project branch, not only when it needed conflict resolution.
  Evidence of absence: Step 9 reads “A step 2 sync that needed a conflict resolution changed the project's code after every recorded run, so none of them counts.” but never invalidates on the broader case of any sync that advanced the branch (clean merge commit, fast-forward into a tip that includes default-branch changes). The CHANGELOG entry mirrors the same narrow rule (“a sync that needed a conflict resolution ... triggers one re-dispatch”). Step 2 only records pre-sync head and “whether this sync needed a conflict resolution” — no post-sync head, no advancement check. agents.md (lines 1148-1156) describes the same narrow anchor (“equal to the project head before that stage's sync merge”) and does not mention post-sync-head comparison. PR description bullet says “the audited commit must equal the project head before the read-result stage's sync merge” but never specifies what happens when that sync merge created a new commit. The intended fix therefore stops short of the named threat: the audit's `<sha>` can match the pre-sync head while the merged tree contains un-audited code from default branch.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: Read-result stages reject recorded runs when the sync needed conflict resolution, but do not reject them when a clean sync advances the project branch.
  WHY: If the default branch advances while a security or validation run is in progress, the run's SHA can equal the recorded pre-sync head even though the project branch now contains code the run did not cover.
